tip.mergeReady: **{0}** · all conflicts fixed — finish the merge
tip.noUpstream: **{0}** · branch {1} isn't linked to a remote yet
notify.sameFile: Heads up! {0} changed the same file(s) you're working on: {1}. Pulling now keeps the conflict small.
pull.okLocal: Merged! Got {0} commit(s) from your team — your own work is all still here.
pull.ok: Merged! Got {0} commit(s) from your team.
pull.upToDate: You already have the latest code. Nothing to pull.
pull.mergeConflict: Your commits and your teammate's changed the same lines in {0} file(s). Pick what to keep in each file, save, then press “Finish merge”.
pull.mergeConflictStash: Your uncommitted work is parked safely and comes back right after the merge is finished.
pull.autostashConflict: Your teammate's code is in, but it overlaps work you haven't committed yet in {0} file(s). Don't worry — a backup of your work is kept until you're done. Fix the files, then stage them.
pull.blocked: There are still {0} unresolved file(s) from last time. Finish those first, then pull again.
pull.blockedReady: Conflicts are fixed but the merge isn't finished yet. Press “Finish merge” first.

pull.detached: You're not on a branch right now (detached HEAD). Switch to a branch, then pull.
pull.untracked: You have new file(s) with the same name as file(s) your teammate just added: {0}. Rename or move yours, then try again.
err.auth: Couldn't sign in to the remote. Press Sync once in Source Control to log in, then PushPug can check again.
err.network: Can't reach the remote right now (offline?). PushPug will keep trying.
err.identity: Git doesn't know your name yet. Set user.name and user.email, then try again.
err.locked: Another git command is running (index.lock). Wait a moment and try again.
err.notRepo: This folder is no longer a git repository.
autostash.dropped: All files are fixed — PushPug cleaned up the backup stash for you.
merge.ready: All conflicts in {0} are fixed. Press “Finish merge” to save the merge.
merge.finished: Merge finished. You're up to date!
noRepo: Open a folder that uses git to let PushPug watch it.

alerter.installing: Installing alerter in the terminal. When it finishes, press “Send test” again.
alerter.noBrew: alerter is installed with Homebrew. Install Homebrew first (brew.sh), then try again.
wv.welcome.title: Hi! I'm Pug from PushPug
wv.welcome.body: When a teammate pushes new code, I'll tell you right away and pull it into your project in one click — without losing your work.
wv.welcome.f1: Know the moment a teammate pushes
wv.welcome.f2: Pull in their code with one click
wv.welcome.f3: Your work stays safe; conflicts come with a guide
wv.lang.title: Which language do you prefer?
wv.lang.body: You can change it any time in Settings.
wv.lang.thHint: เป็นกันเอง อ่านง่าย
wv.theme.title: Pick a look
wv.theme.body: Applies to every PushPug screen. Preview it below.
wv.theme.systemHint: Switches with your VS Code theme
wv.notify.title: How should I let you know?
wv.notify.body: Pick as many as you like.
wv.notify.vscodeHint: A pop-up in the corner while you're coding.
wv.notify.desktopHint: A system notification when you're in another app. If VS Code is in front, you only get the VS Code pop-up — never both.
wv.notify.background: Even when VS Code is closed
wv.notify.backgroundHint: I'll set up a small background task on this computer that runs git fetch at the background interval you pick (every 2 minutes in Balanced mode). It never changes your files, and turning it off removes it.
wv.notify.backgroundWin: Uses Windows Task Scheduler (no pop-up windows).
wv.notify.backgroundNo: Available on macOS and Windows only.
wv.test.title: Let's test a notification
wv.test.body: Press the button and look at the corner of your screen.
wv.test.vscodeOnly: Sent inside VS Code. Desktop notifications aren't available on this computer.
wv.test.mac2: Find “Visual Studio Code” (or “alerter”) and turn on Allow notifications
wv.test.mac3: Set the alert style to Persistent so it stays until you click
wv.test.macNoAlerter: For buttons like “Pull in changes” right on the notification, install the small free helper alerter.
wv.test.alerterOk: alerter is installed — notifications will have buttons.
wv.test.win2: Make sure notifications are on for “Visual Studio Code” (or “Windows PowerShell”)
wv.test.win3: Turn off Do not disturb / Focus while you work with your team
wv.test.linux1: PushPug uses notify-send. Install the libnotify package if nothing shows up.
wv.test.linux2: Turn off Do not disturb in your desktop's notification settings
wv.done.title: All set!
wv.done.tip1: Look at the bottom-left status bar: it turns yellow when teammates push. Click it to pull their code in.
wv.done.tip2: Click Pug in the Activity Bar for “My Team”: the timeline, conflicts and help.
wv.done.tip3: Run “PushPug: ตั้งค่าใหม่” from the Command Palette to see this setup again.
wv.team.noRepo.title: No git project open yet
wv.team.noRepo.body: Open a project folder that uses git, or clone one from GitHub. I'll keep an eye on it for you.
wv.team.upToDateSub: I'll tell you the moment a teammate pushes.
wv.team.pullingSub: Your own work is set aside safely while this runs.
wv.team.successSub: Got {0} commit(s). Your own work is all still here.
wv.team.sameFileBody: {0} changed files you're editing too. Pull now to keep conflicts small.
wv.team.noUpstream.title: This branch isn't on GitHub yet
wv.team.noUpstream.body: Publish branch “{0}” once and I'll start watching it for teammates' pushes.
wv.team.detached.title: You're not on a branch
wv.team.detached.body: Switch to a branch (like main) and I'll start watching it.
wv.team.error.title: I couldn't check just now
wv.team.conflict.merge: Your commits and your teammate's changed the same lines
wv.team.conflict.autostash: Your teammate's code overlaps work you haven't committed yet
wv.team.conflict.mergeSub: Pick what to keep in each file below, save, then finish the merge.
wv.team.conflict.autostashSub: Their code is in. A backup of your work is kept until you finish — fix each file, then stage it (+ in Source Control). I'll clean up the backup automatically.
wv.team.conflict.ready: Every file is fixed. Finish the merge to save it.
wv.team.help.title: What do the buttons mean?
wv.team.help.both: keep both, one after the other — then tidy up by hand if needed.
wv.team.help.mergeIncoming: keep your teammate's version (what they pushed).
wv.team.help.autoCurrent: keep your teammate's version (it's already in your project now).
wv.team.help.tip: Not sure? Choose Accept Both, then read the result and delete what you don't need.
mode.fast.detail: Every 10 s — for teams that push all the time
mode.balanced.detail: Every 30 s — right for most people (default)
mode.batterySaver.detail: Every 60 s — slows down more when idle or on battery
mode.custom.detail: Set every value yourself in PushPug Settings
mode.pickPlaceholder: How often should PushPug check for new code?
sched.pluggedIn: Checking every {0} (plugged in, so the normal pace)
sched.lowBattery: Checking every {0} right now because the battery is at {1}%
sched.idle: Checking every {0} right now because the computer has been idle for {1} min
sched.lowPowerMode: Checking every {0} right now because Low Power Mode / Battery Saver is on
sched.paused: Paused — outside your checking hours. Starts again at {0}
clamp.time: {0}: “{1}” isn't a time like 08:00, so PushPug uses {2}.
settings.resetDone: All PushPug settings are back to their defaults.
wv.freq.title: How often should I check?
wv.freq.body: Faster means you hear about pushes sooner; slower saves battery. Change it any time.
wv.freq.more: Fine-tune every value in PushPug Settings
wv.mode.fast.for: For teams that push all day and want to know right away
wv.mode.batterySaver.for: On battery a lot? Slows down even more when you're away
wv.est.note: For {0} open project(s). Measured: one up-to-date git fetch to GitHub ≈ 5.5 KB (+58 bytes per branch/tag on the remote).
wv.set.title: PushPug Settings
wv.set.sub: Changes apply right away — no restart needed.
wv.set.notify.sameFile: Extra warning for the same file
wv.set.notify.sameFileHint: When a teammate changed a file you're also changing.
wv.set.notify.tested: Sent! Look at the corner of your screen.
wv.set.customHint: Change any value and the mode switches to Custom for you.
wv.set.check: While you work in VS Code
wv.set.checkHint: git fetch of every open project.
wv.set.backgroundHint: Used only when “Even when VS Code is closed” is on.
wv.set.actions: GitHub Actions results while tests run
wv.set.actionsHint: Only while a run is in progress for the latest commit.
wv.set.saverHint: These only ever slow checks down. When several apply, the slowest wins.
wv.set.idle: Haven't touched the computer for {0} min → check every {1}
wv.set.lowBattery: Battery below {0}% and not plugged in → check every {1}
wv.set.lowPower: Low Power Mode / Battery Saver on → check every {0}
wv.set.plugged: Plugged in → always the normal interval
wv.set.hoursHint: Outside these hours PushPug pauses (VS Code and background). “Check now” still works.
wv.set.gh.actionsHint: After every push, tell me whether GitHub's checks passed; show each commit's checks in My Team.
wv.set.gh.signedIn: Signed in through VS Code — private repos and fast polling work.
wv.set.gh.signedOut: Not signed in. Sign in to get GitHub checks for public and private repos.
wv.set.gh.avatarsHint: Commit authors' GitHub pictures in My Team, loaded from GitHub.
checks.auth.ask: PushPug can show the GitHub checks (tests) of every commit. Sign in to GitHub through VS Code to turn this on?
checks.auth.off: OK — GitHub checks are off. Turn them on any time in PushPug Settings → GitHub.
checks.team.failed: The code {0} pushed is failing its checks — maybe don't pull it yet
gerr.rejected.title: Your push was turned away: the remote has commits you don't have yet.
gerr.rejected.fix: Pull in your teammates' code first, then push again.
gerr.auth.title: Git couldn't sign in to the remote.
gerr.auth.fix: Press Sync once in Source Control to sign in (or check your SSH key / token), then try again.
gerr.repoNotFound.title: The remote repository wasn't found, or you don't have access to it.
gerr.repoNotFound.fix: Check the repository URL and that your account has access.
gerr.noUpstream.title: This branch isn't linked to a remote branch yet.
gerr.noUpstream.fix: Publish it once: Source Control → Publish Branch.
gerr.detached.title: You're not on a branch (detached HEAD).
gerr.detached.fix: Switch to a branch (e.g. main) before pulling or pushing.
gerr.mergeInProgress.title: A merge isn't finished yet.
gerr.mergeInProgress.fix: Fix the conflicted files, stage them, then press “Finish merge”.
gerr.rebaseInProgress.title: A rebase is in progress.
gerr.rebaseInProgress.fix: Finish it (git rebase --continue) or cancel it (git rebase --abort) first.
gerr.localChanges.title: Your uncommitted changes would be overwritten.
gerr.localChanges.fix: Commit or stash them first — or use PushPug's “Pull in changes”, which sets them aside safely.
gerr.untrackedOverwritten.title: New files of yours have the same names as files coming in.
gerr.untrackedOverwritten.fix: Rename or move your files, then try again.
gerr.unrelatedHistories.title: These two histories have nothing in common.
gerr.unrelatedHistories.fix: This usually means the wrong remote. Check the repository URL before forcing anything.
gerr.diverged.title: Your branch and the remote both have new commits, and Git wasn't told how to combine them.
gerr.diverged.fix: Use PushPug's “Pull in changes” — it merges them for you.
gerr.identity.title: Git doesn't know your name and e-mail yet.
gerr.identity.fix: Run: git config --global user.name "Your Name" and git config --global user.email you@example.com
gerr.locked.title: Another git command is running (or one crashed and left a lock).
gerr.locked.fix: Wait a moment and try again. If it keeps happening, delete .git/index.lock.
gerr.network.title: Can't reach the remote right now.
gerr.network.fix: Check your internet connection; PushPug will retry by itself.
gerr.notRepo.title: This folder isn't a git repository.
gerr.notRepo.fix: Open the project folder that contains .git.
gerr.unknown.title: Git reported an error.
gerr.unknown.fix: See the full message for details.
push.behind: Teammates pushed {0} new commit(s) since your last pull ({1}). Pushing now would be turned away.
push.nothing: Nothing to push — the remote already has all your commits.
push.rejected: The push was turned away because someone pushed first. Merge their commits in, then push again — PushPug can do both.
undo.none: There's no recent merge to undo.
undo.ok: Undone — your project is back to how it was before the merge, uncommitted work included.
undo.expired: It's been more than 10 minutes, so the merge can't be undone automatically anymore.
undo.committed: You've committed since the merge, so undoing it now could lose that work. Nothing was changed.
undo.changed: You've edited files since the merge, so undoing it now could lose those edits. Nothing was changed.
wv.team.checks.title: Checks
wv.team.check.noLog: No log available here (not a GitHub Actions job, or not signed in to GitHub).
wv.team.check.kind.tests: Some tests failed. Run the tests on your machine to see which ones, fix them, and push again.
wv.team.check.kind.install: Installing dependencies failed — often a package version that doesn't exist, or a lockfile out of date.
wv.team.check.kind.lint: The code-style (lint) check failed. Run the linter (e.g. npm run lint) and fix what it reports.
wv.team.check.kind.timeout: The job ran out of time — something hung or got much slower.
wv.team.check.kind.build: The build or type check failed. Run the build on your machine to see the error.
wv.team.undoHint: Puts everything back as it was, uncommitted work included · {0} left
wv.gh.title: Get GitHub test results?
wv.gh.body: After every push — yours or a teammate's — I'll tell you whether GitHub's checks passed, and show what broke when they don't.
wv.gh.signedIn: Signed in — GitHub checks are on.
wv.gh.private: Uses VS Code's own GitHub sign-in. The token stays in VS Code; PushPug never saves it.
wv.gh.onPass: Also tell me when checks pass
wv.gh.bgNo: While VS Code is closed, checks are included only if the GitHub CLI (gh) is installed and signed in. Otherwise you get them when VS Code is open.
wv.gh.bgYes: GitHub CLI (gh) found and signed in — alerts while VS Code is closed include checks too.
wv.set.quietHint: No pop-ups or desktop notifications during these hours. The status bar keeps updating.
push.protected: This branch only accepts pull requests, so the push was turned away. Send your commits for review instead: PushPug puts them on their own branch and opens the pull request.
gerr.protectedBranch.title: This branch is protected: changes have to go through a pull request.
gerr.protectedBranch.fix: Use "Send for Review": PushPug moves your commits to a branch of their own and opens a pull request.
pr.btn.moveCommits: Put them in the new task
pr.closed: Pull request #{0} was closed without merging.
pr.conflictBody: Someone changed the same lines. Get the latest main into your branch, fix the conflicts, then send again.
pr.noBase: PushPug can't find the team's main branch on the remote. Publish the repository first.
pr.badName: That can't be a branch name. Try a few plain words.
pr.nameExists: A branch with that name already exists. Pick another description.
pr.conflictFirst: Finish the merge that's in progress first (see My Team).
pr.localChanges: Your uncommitted changes would be overwritten ({0}). Commit or undo them first, then try again.
pr.start.title: Start a new task
pr.start.prompt: What will you work on? A few words become the branch name.
pr.start.hasCommits: You have {0} commit(s) on {1} that weren't sent yet. Put them in this new task so they go into its pull request?
pr.start.ok: You're on {0}, made from the latest {1}. Work and commit as usual, then press "Send for review".
pr.start.movedOk: Your commits are now on {0}, and your {1} matches the team's again. Send them for review?
pr.send.uncommitted: {0} file(s) aren't committed yet, so they won't be in the pull request.
pr.send.nothing: Nothing to send: this branch has no commits that {0} doesn't have.
pr.send.rejected: The branch on GitHub has commits you don't have (maybe someone updated it). Merge them in, then send again — PushPug can do both.
pr.send.pushedOnly: Pushed {0}. This remote isn't on GitHub, so open the pull request on your Git host's website.
pr.send.finishOnGitHub: Pushed {0}. Press "Create pull request" on GitHub to finish.
pr.send.opened: Pull request #{0} is open. Your team can look at it now.
pr.updated: Merged the latest {0} into your branch. Send it again so the pull request updates.
pr.finish.notMerged: This pull request isn't merged yet. Switch to {0} anyway? Your branch {1} stays as it is.
pr.finish.ok: Back on {0} with the latest code. Deleted the finished branch {1}.
pr.finish.kept: Back on {0}. Branch {1} was kept because it has work that isn't merged.
wv.team.pr.onBaseHint: Start a task to work on your own branch and send it as a pull request.
wv.team.pr.unsentHint: {1} only takes pull requests? PushPug moves these commits to their own branch and opens one.
wv.team.pr.none: Not sent for review yet · {0} commit(s)
wv.team.pr.noCommits: No commits yet. Commit your work, then send it for review.
wv.team.pr.open: Pull request #{0} is waiting for review
